case.case_title: Rajakaruna v. De Silva, Minister of Housing, Construction and Public Utilities and Others
case.source_citation: Supreme Court of Sri Lanka, S.C. Application No. 201/95, decided on 9 May 1997

clause.text: No citizen shall be discriminated against on the grounds of race, religion, language, caste, sex, political opinion, place of birth or any one of such grounds.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the petitioner was discriminated against on political grounds in violation of Article 12(2) of the Constitution.
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner claimed he was singled out and discriminated against as a supporter of the United National Party due to a letter he wrote to the then President.
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondents argued there was no evidence of political discrimination; the petitioner was actually a supporter of the present Government and was not singled out.
key_facts: Petitioner wrote a letter to the then President expressing support for the United National Party.
Petitioner was Vice President of a union supporting the present Government.
No material evidence showed petitioner’s involvement with the United National Party beyond the letter.
Petitioner’s appeals against transfer were rejected on service grounds, not political grounds.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The court interpreted Article 12(2) as prohibiting discrimination on political grounds but required material evidence to prove such discrimination.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The court found no material evidence that the petitioner was victimized or discriminated against due to political affiliation; rather, evidence suggested he supported the present Government.
principles_established: Discrimination claims under Article 12(2) require material evidence of discrimination on listed grounds.
Political affiliation must be clearly established to prove discrimination under Article 12(2).

outcome.holding: The court held that the petitioner’s fundamental rights under Article 12(2) were not violated as there was no proof of political discrimination.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 12(2) was directly engaged by the petitioner’s claim of political discrimination, and the court’s dismissal was based on the absence of evidence to support such discrimination.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The petitioner was found to be a supporter of the present Government and no material evidence showed discrimination due to political affiliation.
